isViewer.description:
Hide this button when the document is open read-only. Opt-out: read as `isViewer !== false`,
so the button shows in viewer mode unless this is `false`.

Note the opposite sense of {@link VariationConfig.isViewer}, which is opt-in and defaults to
hidden. Same name, same file, inverted default.

group.description:
Places the plugin in its own group in the **Plugins** tab, separated from the rest. Omitted,
the plugin joins the last group. Read as `item.group.name` / `item.group.rank`.

help.description: A help/support link for the plugin.

offered.description: The plugin author who proposed the plugin for publication.

onlyofficeScheme.description: On desktop editors, serves the plugin through the `onlyoffice://` custom scheme instead of `file://`, so it gets a real origin with working CORS and a secure context.

version.description:
The plugin's own version, e.g. `"1.0"`. Optional per the reference, and genuinely omitted by
shipped plugins - `guid`, `name` and `variations` are the only required top-level fields.

PluginKeyword.description: One word or short phrase people type into the marketplace search.

PluginKeywords.description:
Search words for one language - kept short so the list names what the plugin does rather than
every popular term.

keywords.description:
Words the marketplace search finds the plugin by, besides its name. A plain array is searched
whatever the interface language. An object maps a language to its own words, keyed like
`nameLocale` (`ru`, `pt-BR`); a search typed in Latin letters also looks at the `en` words.

platforms.description:
Where the plugin works: `web` - the editors in a browser, `desktop` - the desktop editors, in
either of their modes (local files or a connected cloud). Omit it when the plugin works
everywhere.

ToolbarDisableReason.description:
A reason for disabling the editor toolbar, as `VariationConfig.disableReasons` and the
`onChangeToolbarDisableReasons` event name it. More may be added in future versions.

buttons.description: Defaults to no buttons (an empty toolbar) when omitted - routinely omitted in practice.

disableReasons.description:
The reasons for disabling the editor toolbar that also disable the plugin button. If it is not
specified, any reason disables the button. While the document is loading or being refreshed,
or the About panel is open, the button is always disabled. Read from the first variation only.

icons.description: Some plugins use the same rich per-scale shape here as `icons2` instead of a plain path/map.
icons.signature: icons?: Record<string, string> | string[] | string | IconConfig[];

isActivated.description:
Whether the created panel starts expanded (`true`, the default) or collapsed (`false`).

Panel variations only - `type` of `"panel"` or `"panelRight"`. The side-menu button and the
panel are created either way; `false` only skips expanding it on render, leaving the user to
open it from the button. Read as `isActivated !== false`, so omitting it and setting it to
`true` are the same - only `false` does anything.

isDisplayedInViewer.description:
Hide a viewer-enabled variation from the viewer's plugin list after all. Only consulted when
`isViewer` is `true`, and read as `isDisplayedInViewer !== false`.

isViewer.description:
Offer this variation when the document is open read-only. Opt-in, default `false`: in edit
mode a variation is listed regardless, and in viewer mode only `isViewer: true` puts it
there - subject to `isDisplayedInViewer`, which can hide it again.

The editor's test is `isEdit || isViewer && isDisplayedInViewer !== false`. Note that
{@link ButtonConfig.isViewer} is the opposite: opt-out, shown unless set to `false`.

isVisual.description: Omitted in practice about as often as it's set explicitly.

methods.description: executeMethod names this variation calls - purely descriptive/documentation, not enforced.

screens.description: Store listing screenshots for this specific variation (see also StoreConfig.screenshots).

attachEditorEvent.description:
Per-editor overloads (typed from each editor's own plugin-events.js) come first so a known
event name gets its real payload type; the events shared by all editors
(common/base-plugin-events.js - onChangeToolbarDisableReasons, onFloatActionButtonClick, ...) are
typed from `PluginEventMap`, the same map `attachEvent` uses, since both receive the same
editor `onEvent` message; the final overload is a loose fallback for events not modeled yet.

callCommand.description:
Runs `command` inside the editor's process, where the global `Api` is the entry point.

The function is serialized with `Function.prototype.toString()`, so it is **not a closure**:
nothing from the surrounding scope is visible inside it. Pass data in through
`Asc.scope` (JSON-serialized into the command's context and readable there as `Asc.scope` or
the bare `scope`) rather than by capturing variables.

`command`'s return value is delivered to `callback`. It must be plain data - see
{@link CommandSerializable}; returning an `Api.*` object yields `undefined` at runtime and is
rejected here at compile time.

callCommandAsync.description:

functions. Always runs with `isClose: false` and `isCalc: true`; use `callCommand` directly
when you need either of those to differ.

executeMethod.description:
The first alternative covers the `@undocumented` methods - real and callable, outside
ONLYOFFICE's published surface and its compatibility promise. See `./undocumented` for what
each one does and why it is declared by hand; the same map types them on the global
`Editor`, so the two channels cannot drift apart. The rest is one alternative per editor.

The whole chain has to start on this line: the ambient-bundle builder recognizes an
overload chain by `name: (signature) &` and prunes the four foreign editors out of it
(`pruneEditorOverloads`), and it stops recognizing the chain if the first signature is
moved onto a line of its own.

ignoreDisabledToolbar.description:
Keep the toolbar button enabled while the editor toolbar is disabled, so the plugin decides
its state itself - from the `onChangeToolbarDisableReasons` event, through `disabled`. Default
`false`: the editor disables the button together with the toolbar.

Toolbar buttons only. While the document is loading or being refreshed, or the About panel is
open, the editor disables the button anyway.

onContextMenuShowAnalyze.description:
Called first, every time the menu is about to be shown. Return `true` to drop this button
from this particular menu - the editor then skips it and all of its children, before the
`showOnOptionsType` and `EditorsSupport` tests run at all.

Override to decide per invocation, from `options` or from where the button would be placed.
The default implementation returns `false`, so nothing is dropped.

onContextMenuShowExtendItem.description:
Called once the item has been built and before it is pushed into the parent's `items`, so a
mutation here lands in the menu the editor renders. Children are processed afterwards.

Use it to adjust text, `disabled` or `pressed` per invocation; returning anything is
pointless, as `onContextMenuShow` ignores the result.

CommandSerializable.description:
Rejects anything a `callCommand` result can't survive.

The command body is serialized with `Function.prototype.toString()` and re-run inside the
editor's own process, so its return value has to cross a process boundary. The editor filters it
through `Asc.checkReturnCommand`, which walks the value up to 10 levels deep and replaces
anything carrying methods - an `ApiParagraph`, an `ApiDocument`, any other `Api.*` object - with
`undefined`. Mapping function-valued properties to `never` turns that silent data loss into a
compile error, while plain data (object literals, interfaces, arrays, unions, nested
combinations) passes through untouched.

ContextMenuItems.description:
What `AddContextMenuItem`/`UpdateContextMenuItem` take: the plugin's own guid and its entries.

sdkjs's JSDoc says `@param {ContextMenuItem[]} items`, but the implementation reads
`items["guid"]` and `items["items"]` off the one argument, and the plugins.js button helper sends
exactly this object - `executeMethod("AddContextMenuItem", [{ guid, items }])`.

items.description: The entries to show; an empty array shows none, which still answers the request.

footer.description: Word only. Set when the cursor is in a footer that is being edited.

footerArea.description: Word only. Set when the menu was opened over the footer area of the page.

guid.description:
With `type: "OleObject"`: the guid of the plugin the OLE object belongs to, so a plugin can
offer its own entries only on its own objects (`options.guid === Asc.plugin.info.guid`).

header.description: Word only. Set when the cursor is in a header that is being edited.

headerArea.description: Word only. Set when the menu was opened over the header area of the page.

type.description:
What the menu was opened on (sdkjs `Asc.c_oPluginContextMenuTypes`): `"Target"` - the cursor
with nothing selected, `"Selection"` - selected text, `"Image"`, `"Shape"`, `"OleObject"`, or
`"None"`.

ContextMenuShowItem.description:
One entry of the menu as the `Asc.Buttons` helper layer builds it - the object `toItem()` returns
and the two hooks below are handed. Only `id` and `text` are always present; every other field is
written only when the matching property is set on the button.

Not the same shape as the generated `ContextMenuItem`, which is what `executeMethod`'s
`AddContextMenuItem` accepts: this one carries the helper's own `hint`, `separator`,
`lockInViewMode`, `ignoreDisabledToolbar`, `enableToggle` and `pressed`, and has no `icons`.

InputHelper.description:
A window that appears and disappears as the user types, positioned against the cursor. Obtained
from `Asc.plugin.getInputHelper()` after `Asc.plugin.createInputHelper()`.

getScrollSizes.description:
Returns the scrollable size of the input helper window.

Keyed `w`/`h`, not `width`/`height`: sdkjs's own JSDoc declares this `@returns {number}` and
describes it as "width and height", but the implementation returns `{ w, h }` - the shape
here follows the implementation.

Fired when a text annotation (e.g. a grammar/spellcheck range) loses focus. * * @requires ONLYOFFICE Docs Developer Edition. Annotations are not present in other * builds, where this event is never fired. * @since 9.2.0 */ onBlurAnnotation: [annotation: TextAnnotation]; /** * Word only. data.description:
What the editor sent the plugin at launch, shaped by the variation's `initDataType`: the
selected text for `"text"`, HTML for `"html"`, and so on. The same value `init` receives as
its argument, which is the usual way to read it.

height.description: With `objectId`: the object's height in millimetres.

heightPix.description: With `objectId`: the object's height in pixels, as last drawn by the plugin.

objectId.description:
Set when the plugin is opened on an OLE object it owns (`initDataType: "ole"`), e.g. by a
double click: the object's internal id, to pass back when editing that object
(`EditOleObject`). `data` then holds the object's own data string. Written by sdkjs's
`COleObject.convertDataObjectToPluginData`, as are the four sizes below.

options.description:
Replaced wholesale whenever the host sends `updateOptions`, just before
{@link AscPlugin.onUpdateOptions} fires. The payload is whatever that host chose to send, so
it carries no shape the editor guarantees.

recalculate.description:
Set by the runtime around a command issued from a plugin window, and read by the editor to
decide whether to recalculate after it. Not something a plugin assigns.

width.description: With `objectId`: the object's width in millimetres.

widthPix.description: With `objectId`: the object's width in pixels, as last drawn by the plugin.

prototype.description:
Only present on the initial `Asc.scope` the runtime bootstraps (`plugins.dev.js` sets it once
at startup as a convenience for plugin authors - the runtime itself never calls it). Plugins
routinely replace `Asc.scope` wholesale with a plain data payload before `callCommand`
(`window.Asc.scope = { foo: 1 }`) so that data is readable inside the sandboxed callback -
that payload has no reason to carry `prototype.clear`, so it must stay optional here.

activate.description: Brings the window forward, and focuses it when `isFocus` is set.

attachEvent.description:
Subscribes to what the window's own page sends with `Asc.plugin.sendToPlugin(eventName,
data)`. The payload is whatever that page sent, so the plugin names its type: `T` is the
caller's statement of the protocol between its two pages, not something the runtime checks.
attachEvent.signature: attachEvent: <T = unknown>(eventName: string, callback: (data: T) => void) => void;

ActivateWindow.description: Brings a plugin window or panel forward - what `PluginWindow.activate` sends.

AddContextMenuItem.description:
Adds the plugin's entries to the context menu that is opening. The answer to
`onContextMenuShow`: a plugin that listens for that event must call this every time, with an
empty `items` array when it has nothing to add, or the editor keeps waiting for it before it
shows the menu. Clicks arrive through `attachContextMenuClickEvent(id, ...)`.

AddToolbarMenuItem.description:
Adds toolbar tabs and buttons for the plugin. Clicks arrive through
`attachToolbarMenuClickEvent(id, ...)`.

One object, not an array: sdkjs's JSDoc says `ToolbarMenuMainItem[]` and the office-js-api
example passes `[[item]]`, but the implementation reads `items["guid"]` and `items["tabs"]`
directly, and the plugins.js button helper sends `[{ guid, tabs }]`.

CloseWindow.description:
Closes a plugin modal window. `windowId` is the window's `PluginWindow.id` (a GUID string)
or the `windowID` the window's `button` call reports - sdkjs's own `PluginWindow.close` sends
`executeMethod("CloseWindow", [this.id])`.

OnWindowDockChangedCallback.description:
Acknowledges an `onDockedChanged` window event.

Not a utility to call on its own - it is the second half of a handshake. When the window's
docked state changes, the editor parks a callback under
`dockCallbacks[pluginGuid + "_" + windowId]` and sends the plugin an `onWindowEvent` with
`eventName: "onDockedChanged"`. Calling this runs that callback and deletes it, so the
editor can finish what it was waiting on. Calling it with no pending callback does nothing.

ResizeWindow.description:
Resizes the plugin modal window.

sdkjs's own JSDoc for `pluginMethod_ResizeWindow` types size/minSize/maxSize as plain
`number`, but the web runtime (`onPluginWindowResize` in web-apps' Plugins.js) reads
`size[0]`/`size[1]` and `minSize.length`/`maxSize[0]` - all three are `[width, height]`
pairs on the wire, which is also how every real caller (e.g. the antidote and mendeley
plugins) passes them. minSize/maxSize are omitted when only resizing, and the callback
fires with `"resize_result"` once the window has been resized.
ResizeWindow.signature: ResizeWindow: [ frameId: string, size: [width: number, height: number], minSize?: [width: number, height: number], maxSize?: [width: number, height: number], ];

ShowButton.description: Shows or hides one of the plugin's own buttons.
ShowButton.signature: ShowButton: [buttonId: string, visible: boolean, align?: string];

UpdateContextMenuItem.description:
Replaces the plugin's entries in a context menu that is already open, e.g. once an
asynchronous check decides what to offer.

UpdateToolbarMenuItem.description: Replaces the plugin's toolbar items added by `AddToolbarMenuItem`, matched by id.

UndocumentedMethodReturnMap.description:
What the callback receives, by method name.

Only `ResizeWindow` carries a value: it is the one of these that calls
`setPluginMethodReturnAsync()` and later answers `onPluginMethodReturn("resize_result")`. The
others return synchronously, so their callback fires with nothing - which is still worth
declaring, because the Promise form (`await Editor.CloseWindow(win.id)`) resolves at that moment.

AscDesktopEditor.description:
The ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editor bridge, present only when the plugin runs in the desktop app -
hence `AscDesktopEditor | undefined` on the global.

Not reachable inside `Asc.plugin.callCommand`: that body runs in the editor's own scope, where the
editor rebinds this name to an empty object. Read what you need in the plugin frame and pass it in
through `Asc.scope`.

LocalFileSave.signature: LocalFileSave(params: string, password: string, docinfo?: unknown, fileType?: number, jsonOptions?: string, passwordOld?: string): void;

LocalFileSaveChanges.signature: LocalFileSaveChanges(changes: string, deleteIndex: number, count: number): void;

OpenFilenameDialog.signature: OpenFilenameDialog(type: DesktopDialogType, multiple: boolean, callback: (file: string | string[]) => void): void;

error.signature: error?: (response: any, status: string, error: any) => void;
